findings.evidence: InvariantMass.lean:182-185 declares `{γ : PhotonKinematics}` with hypotheses only on `q.timeComponent`/`q.spatialPart`; `grep virtuality InvariantMass.lean` returns no hit. Kinematics/Basic.lean:69-71 states the convention being broken: the virtuality is 'carried explicitly so that a photoproduction statement is a statement about `Q² → 0` rather than about an implicit `Q² = 0`'; the roadmap §0.1 likewise asks that the photon be 'described by its energy in the collider frame and its virtuality, both explicit' (roadmap/EpsilonEridaniRoadmaps/Photoproduction/README.md:309-313).
findings.fix: Tie `q` to `γ` as a whole: add `hγ : γ.virtuality = -⟪q, q⟫ₘ` to the `EnergyFraction` section variables (this is what `PhotonKinematics.ofEmission` already sets definitionally), expose the resulting `γ.IsReal` as a lemma derived from `hn`/`hq`/`hq'`, and give the energy-fraction form of the general `W² = M² + q² + 2(q⁰E + p q_∥)` in terms of `γ.virtuality` so the virtuality stays explicit.
findings.issue: `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_realPhoton_energyFraction` and `energyFraction_eq_exp_rapidity_mul` (line 199) take `γ : PhotonKinematics` but use only `γ.energy`; `γ.virtuality` is never mentioned or constrained. The names and docstrings say 'real photon', yet realness is smuggled in through the shape of `q` (`hq`/`hq'` force `⟪q,q⟫ₘ = 0`) while the record may carry `γ.virtuality ≠ 0`. Nothing in the file ever links `γ.virtuality` to `⟪q,q⟫ₘ`, so the virtuality-explicit `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_target` cannot be stated through the `PhotonKinematics` API at all.

findings.evidence: Rapidity.lean:47-48 takes an arbitrary `n : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` with no `‖n‖ = 1`; every collinear lemma in the file (lines 95, 102, 112, 127, 143, 151) and every downstream use in InvariantMass.lean (lines 112, 182, 217) carries `hn : ‖n‖ = 1`, so unit `n` is the intended convention. `real_inner_smul_right` (used at InvariantMass.lean:87) gives the scaling identity.
findings.fix: State in the `rapidity` docstring (and the module docstring) that it is the rapidity along `n` only when `‖n‖ = 1`, and add the public scaling lemma `rapidity v (c • n) = artanh (c * ⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫_ℝ / v.timeComponent)` so the dependence is part of the interface rather than an unstated convention.
findings.issue: `rapidity v n = artanh (⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫ / v⁰)` is documented as the rapidity 'along the spatial direction `n`' (line 46, and module docstring line 14), but it is the physical rapidity only for `‖n‖ = 1`: by linearity of the real inner product, `rapidity v (c • n) = artanh (c * ⟪v.spatialPart, n⟫ / v⁰) ≠ rapidity v n`. The definition carries no normalization hypothesis and the file has no lemma recording the scaling, so a consumer passing an unnormalized axis gets a silently wrong number.

summary: The characteristic API for the new `rapidity` definition is complete and bodies stay hidden, but two public statements are misleading: the `PhotonKinematics` bridge lemmas silently assume the photon is real while leaving `γ.virtuality` entirely unconstrained, and `rapidity` is documented as a quantity 'along a direction' though its value scales with `‖n‖` with no lemma or hypothesis recording that.
